11.4a — MC Strategy + Practice Set 1

70 questions, 120 minutes — about 100 seconds each, no penalty for guessing. Today is not about learning new content; it is about a STRATEGY for a 2-hour sprint, plus your first full-conditions practice set. Read the strategy guide first.

Strategy ~15 min

The three-pass method:

  1. Pass 1 (fast, ~60 min): answer every question you know instantly. Flag the rest — NO lingering. A skipped question costs 100 seconds; a lingered one costs 300 and steals the same points from later questions
  2. Pass 2 (~40 min): the flagged ones you can eliminate on. Wrong answers have TELLS — read them before solving
  3. Pass 3 (~20 min): what remains. Answer EVERYTHING. No penalty = guessing is free points; an empty bubble is the only wrong choice

Wrong-answer tells you already know from this class:

  • Off-by-one options (loop runs n vs n-1 times — the exam builds distractors from off-by-one mistakes)
  • "Always/never" absolutes (rarely true — the world runs on tradeoffs, 9.3a)
  • Right answer with wrong REASON (two options say "10"; only one says why) — the "why" options test whether you traced the code or guessed the number
  • Binary/hex conversion options with transposed digits (9.2a's 0x1F vs 0xF1 — they KNEW that was your error)

Socratic

The MC section includes some questions about "innovations' impacts" (IOC-1) with no code in them. Where does the time you save by bubbling fast on tracing questions go — and why is a 100-second average a LIE (some questions need 30s, some need 180)?

Practice Set 1 ~30 min

Set 1: 15 questions, 15 minutes, timed strictly. Your teacher hands out Set 1 (or posts it) — a mix across the CED families. Track per question:

  • Family (data? algorithms? networks? systems? impact?)
  • Your time: instant / eliminator / guess
  • Right or wrong

The scorecard matters more than the score. Grade, then build your error table: which FAMILY bleeds points? Your answer decides your homework — and the next two classes target it (11.4b data and networks, 11.4c algorithms and systems).

Bug Hunt: Strategy bugs

  1. You got 11/15 — and spent 4 minutes on one question you still missed. What does the math say about that trade (4 minutes = 2.4 easy questions elsewhere)?
  2. You changed 3 answers at the end, 2 were wrong changes. What does research say about first instincts (they beat panicked revisions — when do you change: only with a REASON found afterward)?
  3. Your error table is all one family. What is tonight's study plan — and why is "study everything" the wrong plan this close to the exam?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain the three-pass method and the 100-second average's lie
  • Name three wrong-answer tells and spot them in Set 1
  • Show your error table with families and times
  • Have a study plan targeting your weakest family
